title: The Invisible Web: The Geopolitics of Subsea Cables
subtitle: Understanding the fragile physical infrastructure that powers the global internet.
description: While we often think of the internet as 'the cloud,' nearly all global data travels through physical cables on the ocean floor. This series explores how these critical lifelines have become the new frontier of international security, economic competition, and geopolitical tension.

articles.label: Part 1
articles.note: Explain the history and function of subsea cables as the 'highways' of the modern internet.

articles.label: Part 2
articles.note: Examine the shift from telecom-led projects to big tech (Google, Meta, Amazon) ownership.

articles.label: Part 3
articles.note: Discuss recent incidents of cable damage and the fear of state-sponsored sabotage.

articles.label: Part 4
articles.note: Focus on the specific challenges for island nations like Taiwan regarding connectivity and resilience.

articles.label: Part 5
articles.note: Explore emerging solutions like satellite internet (Starlink) and international regulatory efforts.
